observations.text: SP, due to an unrehearsed go-around flow, did not apply climb power and did not clean the A/C configuration in the standardized order at the missed approach point, raising the gear before the climb attitude was set. The published missed approach track was not intercepted, with the result that the radial deviation reached 12 degrees and the IP had to direct the climb and fly part of the turn to the holding fix. Further study of the missed approach procedure in the Techniques and Procedures Manual and in the MAIP is required.

SP, due to attention captured by the approach chart at the expense of the instrument cross-check, did not execute the missed approach at the published missed approach point and did not clean the A/C configuration within the airspeed limits. Flap retraction was made with the airspeed 18 knots above the briefed missed approach speed and the aircraft was allowed to go 11 degrees off the missed approach radial, with the result that the IP directed the configuration change and took the aircraft to regain the published track.

SP executed the missed approach to the level required for this stage; however, the transition to the climb attitude and the configuration clean-up were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, and recognition of the drift off the published track was delayed. The radial deviation reached 8 degrees and the climb airspeed was held 15 knots above the briefed value before the correction was made. Marginal performance for the Training Section - timeliness of the missed approach initiation and of the configuration clean-up is expected to improve on the following sorties.

SP executed the missed approach at the published missed approach point without IP prompting, applying climb power and cleaning the A/C configuration in the standardized sequence within the airspeed limits. Minor errors in the turn toward the missed approach track produced a radial deviation of 7 degrees and a climb airspeed 12 knots above the briefed value, both recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP knew the missed approach procedure and executed it timely and without misapprehensions, applying climb power at the missed approach point and cleaning the A/C configuration according to the standardized procedures within the airspeed limits. The published track was intercepted with the radial deviation held inside 4 degrees and the climb airspeed inside 8 knots of the briefed value throughout the transition. No IP prompting or intervention was required. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the missed approach flawlessly, calling the go-around and applying climb power at the missed approach point, then cleaning the A/C configuration in the standardized order well inside the gear and flap limit speeds. Corrections toward the published track were anticipatory, with the radial deviation remaining inside 1 degree and the climb airspeed within 2 knots of the briefed value. Knowledge of the MAIP missed approach and holding entry and the speed of the transition were above the levels desired for this stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to a non-standardized go-around technique, advanced the power lever without setting the climb attitude at the same time and retracted the flaps before the gear at the missed approach point. The A/C settled below the published missed approach altitude and the track was not regained, with the result that the radial deviation exceeded 10 degrees and the IP had to take the aircraft to establish the climb. Further study of the standardized missed approach and of the configuration clean-up sequence is required.

SP, due to inadequate workload management during the approach phase, did not have the navigation aids set up for the missed approach before reaching the missed approach point and did not execute the published turn timely. The climb was flown with the airspeed 20 knots above the briefed missed approach speed while the aircraft drifted 13 degrees off the missed approach radial, with the result that the IP directed the heading and the power setting and flew part of the transition to the holding fix.

SP, due to a delayed transition from the approach scan to the climb scan, did not stabilize the climb attitude on the ADI before turning to the navigation display and did not select the missed approach course in time. The correction toward the published track was made only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the result of a radial deviation of 8 degrees and a climb airspeed 15 knots above the briefed value, recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to failure to monitor the aircraft state after the configuration change, did not detect the airspeed increase while the gear and the flaps were retracted in the climb. The excess reached 15 knots above the briefed missed approach speed and the aircraft was allowed to reach 8 degrees off the missed approach radial before the IP's verbal prompts led to the correction. Recognition of both deviations was delayed.

SP executed the missed approach within the desired standards; however, the configuration clean-up was started before a positive rate of climb was confirmed and the turn toward the missed approach track was begun late on two occasions. The radial deviation reached 6 degrees and the climb airspeed 12 knots above the briefed value, each recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention. Marginal performance for the Training Section - consistency in the sequence of the go-around actions is expected to improve.

SP knew the missed approach procedure and executed it timely and without misapprehensions, applying climb power, setting the climb attitude and cleaning the A/C configuration in the standardized order within the airspeed limits. The published missed approach track was intercepted and held with the radial deviation inside 3 degrees and the climb airspeed inside 5 knots of the briefed value. The go-around call and the holding entry were made without IP prompting. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP executed the missed approach flawlessly and without misapprehensions, transitioning from the approach to the climb at the missed approach point with no break in the instrument cross-check. Configuration clean-up was standardized and well inside the limit speeds, the radial deviation remained negligible at 1 degree and the climb airspeed stayed within 2 knots of the briefed value. Accuracy and speed in the procedure were above the levels desired for this stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.

SP, due to an incorrect set-up of the navigation aids for the missed approach, did not tune and identify the missed approach course before the missed approach point and turned in the direction opposite to the published track. The error was not corrected during the climb, with the result that the radial deviation exceeded 12 degrees and the IP had to direct the reversal and fly part of the transition to the holding fix. Further study of the missed approach segment of the approach plate and of the MAIP holding procedure is required.

SP, due to continuation of the approach after the information that invalidated it had already been received, did not execute the missed approach at the published missed approach point and continued the descent below the missed approach altitude. Climb power was applied late and the A/C configuration was not cleaned within the airspeed limits, the airspeed reaching 18 knots above the briefed missed approach speed and the aircraft 11 degrees off the missed approach radial, with the result that the IP took the aircraft to establish the climb on the published track.

SP, due to a non-standardized go-around flow, did not clean the A/C configuration in the prescribed sequence, delaying the gear retraction until after the flaps were fully up. The turn toward the missed approach track was started only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the result that the radial deviation reached 8 degrees and the climb airspeed 15 knots above the briefed value. Deviations were recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to distraction by radio traffic while established on final, did not execute the missed approach procedure timely at the missed approach point and did not verify the climb attitude before starting the configuration change. Both the interception of the published track and the power setting were completed only after the IP's verbal prompts, with the result of a radial deviation of 8 degrees and a climb airspeed 10 knots below the briefed value during the transition, recognized and corrected with delay.

SP, due to a late transition from the approach scan to the climb scan, did not stabilize the climb attitude before selecting the missed approach course, allowing the aircraft to drift off the published track during the configuration change. The radial deviation reached 7 degrees and the climb airspeed 12 knots above the briefed value, with the result of minor deviations that the SP recognized and corrected in a timely manner without IP intervention.

SP, due to an incomplete mental model of the approach sequence that was not updated when the clearance changed, initially set up the published missed approach instead of the alternate climb-out instruction issued by ATC. The error was recognized on the SP's own re-reading of the clearance and the correct track was regained without IP intervention, with the radial deviation reaching 6 degrees and the climb airspeed 12 knots above the briefed value during the correction.

SP knew and executed the missed approach procedure timely and without misapprehensions, cleaning the A/C configuration according to the standardized procedures and within the airspeed limits; however, the turn toward the missed approach track was begun late on the first of the two missed approaches flown. The radial deviation reached 5 degrees and the climb airspeed 10 knots above the briefed value, both inside the standards for this stage. Marginal performance for the Training Section - promptness of the initial turn is expected to improve on the following sorties.

SP executed the missed approach flawlessly, applying climb power and setting the climb attitude at the missed approach point with no break in the instrument cross-check, then cleaning the A/C configuration in the standardized order well inside the limit speeds. The published track was intercepted without overshoot, with the radial deviation remaining inside 1 degree and the climb airspeed within 2 knots of the briefed value through the transition to the holding fix. The go-around call and the holding entry were made without prompting and knowledge of the MAIP procedure was above the levels desired for this stage. Above end of block MIF achieved.
